scheme_name: Account Aggregator (AA) Framework for FinTech Startups
overview: The Account Aggregator (AA) Framework is an RBI-approved initiative that enables secure, consent-driven sharing of financial data between Financial Information Providers (FIPs) and Financial Information Users (FIUs) via Account Aggregators (AAs). It forms a foundational pillar of India's Digital Public Infrastructure, promoting financial inclusion and innovation across lending, insurance, investments, and personal finance. Sahamati acts as the collective body supporting the AA ecosystem through technical standards, certification, governance, and member services.
objectives: Enable secure, consent-driven sharing of financial data across financial institutions
Promote financial inclusion by expanding access to credit for underserved segments
Strengthen the Account Aggregator ecosystem through technical standards and certification
Support innovation in financial services via open finance principles
Ensure data privacy and user control over personal financial information
Facilitate interoperability among FIPs, AAs, and FIUs through standardized APIs
Drive adoption of Account Aggregator framework across banking, insurance, securities, and pension sectors
eligibility: Any registered and regulated entity under RBI, PFRDA, SEBI, IRDAI, or Department of Revenue (GSTN) can participate in the AA ecosystem as a Financial Information Provider (FIP), Financial Information User (FIU), Account Aggregator (AA), or Technology Service Provider (TSP), provided they obtain certification for their APIs as per Sahamati Certification Guidelines and are 'Live' or 'Ready to go Live' in the AA production environment.
benefits: Members gain access to Sahamati Central Registry (UAT and Production), Common Token Issuance Service, member dashboards (e.g., sAAns), technical health data via APIs, support application access, inter-member dispute resolution framework, implementation/specification assistance, participation in participatory governance forums (Committees and Councils on fair use, economic model, interoperability, fraud prevention), tech working groups, access to Governing Council minutes, advocacy and education benefits including member-driven workshops, on-demand sessions, themed events, and discussion forums.
financial_support: The Account Aggregator Framework does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies to participating entities. Instead, it enables indirect financial benefits by improving access to credit, reducing operational costs in lending and underwriting, and expanding market reach for financial services through consent-based data sharing. For example, AA has enabled loans worth ₹1.6 lakh crore across 1.8+ crore loan accounts as of February 2026.
application_process: 1. Get registered with a Financial Service Regulator (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA, or GSTN). 2. Implement the required module (FIP/FIU/AA/TSP) using RBI-defined API specifications published by ReBIT. 3. Test the module in RBI-approved Account Aggregator Sandboxes. 4. Enrol the module in the UAT-Central Registry for testing in the development environment. 5. Obtain certification from a Sahamati-empanelled auditor for adherence to ReBIT Technical Standards. 6. Get details publicised by Sahamati in the Central Registry upon going live. 7. Launch services with customers.
required_documents: Valid certificate of registration issued by a financial sector regulator
Duly executed copy of the Sahamati Membership Terms
Copy of the authorisation document in favour of the signatory
Proof of certification as per Sahamati Certification Guidelines
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Sahamati – Collective of Account Aggregator Ecosystem
contact_details: Email: membership@sahamati.org.in | For RE membership: memberservices@sahamati.org.in | For certification: services@sahamati.org.in | For Fair Use: fairuse@sahamati.org.in | For SaaNS access: memberservices@sahamati.org.in | For grievances: operations@sahamati.org.in
caveats: All NBFC-AAs must be classified under Fee Category B for membership fees
Entities must align their use cases with Fair Use Template parameters to avoid rejection of consent requests
AA does not store, process, or sell customer data; data is encrypted in transit
Only asset-based data (bank accounts, deposits, mutual funds, insurance policies, pension funds) is currently accessible via AA
Membership fees apply based on entity category and regulator (e.g., Category A: Rs. 5 Lakh, Category B: Rs. 1.25 Lakh, Category C: Rs. 25,000)
Certification is mandatory for participation and must be renewed upon major version changes in ReBIT Technical Specifications or Sahamati Certification Framework
